Incident Bot: [PAGER] control-plane: elevated 5xx rate observed on /v1/org/lookup and /v1/auth/verify (alerts: CP-5xx-Spike) :rotating_light:
Incident Bot: Event time 2026-03-15T02:13:19Z • priority: P1 • routed to oncall-carla • docs: https://runbook.internal/controlplane-5xx
Carla - oncall: on it. paging SRE + infra. seeing ~18% 5xx across control-plane frontends in the last 5m.
Carla - oncall: initial hypothesis: orglookup upstream (cache miss) + auth token validation timeouts causing fanout and cascading 502/504.
Ben (infra): I'm checking the gateway logs now, tailing gateway-prod* - looks like a spike of 502s with backend code 524 from auth-proxy.
Ben (infra): logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:12:58Z gateway-prod-1 svc=controlplane path=/v1/org/lookup upstream=auth-proxy-2 status=502 backend_status=524 latency_ms=2131
2026-03-15T02:13:01Z gateway-prod-3 svc=controlplane path=/v1/auth/verify upstream=billing-auth status=502 backend_status=504 latency_ms=3205
```
Carla - oncall: @Mike can you grab traces for a few requests? want to see which dependency is timing out first.
Mike (SRE): attaching trace links: https://traces.internal/trace/0xA12F... (sample). spans show org-lookup waiting on config-service and then long authz call to billing-auth.
Alice G: I see a config-service scaling event around 02:05 that coincides; pods flapping and OOM-killed, crash loops reported. config-service logs show GC + DB connection exhaustion.
Eva (eng-runtime): worth trying fallback: enable prefix cache for orglookup (serve from local cache) and raise timeouts on gateway -> auth-proxy to avoid cascading. I'll prepare small patch to runtime config.
Carla - oncall: mitigation plan (short):
- Add temporary circuit-breaker on controlplane->config-service to return cached config for 30s (reduce backend load)
- Increase gateway timeout to 6s for auth-proxy calls to let slow calls finish instead of immediate 502s
- Roll scaling to config-service (add 3 replicas) and patch DB pool size config
- If still bad, enable degraded-mode: read-only org lookup cache + disable non-essential billing lookups
Carla - oncall: doing the config changes now. tagging deploy-bot to run config rollout.
deploy-bot: started rollout of runtime-config/controlplane-emergency/20260315-1 by Carla - oncall • 3 steps (validate, apply, verify)
Ben (infra): scaling config-service CRD to 6 replicas now: `kubectl scale deploy/config-service --replicas=6 -n controlplane-prod`
Ben (infra): also bumping DB pool from 20 -> 40 in k8s secret and rollout.
Alice G: watch DB connections, we risk exhausting RDS if surge continues. preparing read-only cache plan.
Mike (SRE): I set a temporary circuit-breaker in envoy: max_connections=2000, consecutive_errors=5, failure_timeout=30s for config-service cluster.
Eva (eng-runtime): pushed runtime config to enable local orglookup prefix cache and extended gateway timeouts.
Carla - oncall: verify steps: run curl against gateway to simulate orglookup with cached key:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer test" https://api.internal/v1/org/lookup?org=acme
```
Carla - oncall: results: responses succeed from cache for many requests; 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 6% in last 3m. :thumbsup:
Ronja (support): we have two customer tickets showing elevated errors (enterprise-acme, big-saas-inc). informing CS lead and sending status note.
Ronja (support): posting interim status to customers: "We're investigating an elevated error rate impacting some control-plane requests; mitigation in progress. Expect updates in 30 minutes."
Ben (infra): after scale + cb + cache, config-service CPU stable but DB connections increased to ~65% usage — within planned bump. No new OOMs.
Mike (SRE): traces now show reduced tail latency for org-lookup; auth verify still has occasional slow calls that come from billing-auth (third-party).
Eva (eng-runtime): can we route some auth verification to a lighter-weight path that validates tokens locally (short-lived cache) to reduce billing-auth calls? I can flip feature flag to use local token cache for 10m.
Carla - oncall: do it. Eva please toggle and post the flag id.
Eva (eng-runtime): toggled ff: controlplane.local_token_cache=true (rollout 100% in 12s). Monitor.
Carla - oncall: 5xx rate now ~2.1% last 2m, error volume trending down. good signal.
Incident Bot: PAGER: control-plane error-rate reduced below threshold; agents: escalation auto-paused.
Carla - oncall: starting handoff notes for next oncall (Ben in 20m). current mitigations:
- Envoy circuit-breaker on config-service (conservative)
- Runtime prefix cache enabled for orglookup
- Gateway timeout extended for auth-proxy calls
- Local token cache feature flag enabled
- Scaled config-service replicas to 6 and adjusted DB pool
Carla - oncall: still see residual 502s to billing-auth at ~0.5% — triggers: external dependency latency. open follow-up with Eng-Billing.
Ben (infra): creating ticket ENG-2312 to investigate billing-auth latency and long-term fixes (retry/backoff improvements, connection pooling).
Alice G: postmortem owners: Carla + Eva + Ben + Mike. I'll schedule a 1hr bridge in 2h to go over root cause and customer impact.
Ronja (support): updating status page: "Mitigation applied; error rates reduced. We're investigating root cause and will update within 2 hours."
Carla - oncall: final checks: runload script shows percentile latency back within SLO for 99th pct. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. Will hand off to Ben for watch.
Carla - oncall: handoff to Ben in 15m. please keep pager unmuted in case of regressions.
Ben (infra): ack — taking watch. will follow up with ENG-2312 and escalate to billing-eng if needed.
Carla - oncall: closing slack thread for live debugging. postmortem to include: sequence of events, why config-service scaled/clashed with DB pool, why billing-auth latency spiked, and proposals (local token validation permanently, better connection pool sizing, circuit-breaker tuning).
deploy-bot: rollout controlplane-emergency/20260315-1 completed successfully • verified checks passed.
Mike (SRE): note for postmortem: we saw a thundering herd of cache misses after config restart. consider warming caches on deploy and soft-start traffic ramp.
Ronja (support): customers notified; three customers acknowledged. no major data loss reported.
Carla - oncall: thanks all, nice quick ops. :clap:
Alice G: saving logs/traces and assigning follow-ups: ENG-2312 (billing-auth), ENG-2313 (config-service tuning), ENG-2314 (postmortem writeup).
Carla - oncall: thread archived for now. if anything spikes, reopen.
